source: Category-level split percentages follow standard ICAR/state agricultural university package-of-practice guidance on basal vs. topdress fertiliser application (e.g. cereals: basal + 2 N topdressings at tillering/CRI and jointing/panicle-initiation, full P and often K basal; legumes: fully basal since the crop fixes its own N once nodulation starts; long-duration cash crops: N split across 3 stages, K split basal + reproductive). This is standard taught practice, not a bespoke per-crop field-trial result - verify against your crop's specific ICAR handbook before real deployment.
note: Each nutrient's percentages across the 5 stage buckets sum to 100. Buckets match AggregatedData.crop_stage_hint.

cereal.description: Wheat, Rice, Maize, Pearl Millet, Sorghum, Barley - basal + 2 N topdressings, P mostly basal, K split basal/reproductive.

legume.description: Soybean, Chickpea, Groundnut, Lentil, Pigeon Pea, Green Gram, Black Gram - starter dose, fully basal; the crop fixes its own N from nodulation onward.

long_duration_cash_crop.description: Cotton, Sugarcane - long season, N split across 3 stages, K split basal + reproductive for boll/cane development.

oilseed_root.description: Mustard, Sunflower, Potato - two-way N split (basal + one topdressing/earthing-up), P and K basal.
